title: Pre-train and Refine: Towards Higher Efficiency in K-Agnostic Community Detection without Quality Degradation

problem.claim: Community detection partitions graph nodes into densely connected groups, but balancing detection quality and efficiency is challenging, especially when the number of communities is unknown.

gap.claim: Existing community detection methods tend to provide either impressive quality or efficiency, leaving a need for a better trade-off in K-agnostic community detection.

contributions.claim: PRoCD reformulates K-agnostic community detection as binary node-pair classification.
PRoCD uses a pre-training and refinement paradigm, with offline pre-training on small synthetic graphs followed by inductive transfer and refinement on large real graphs.
The transferred community detection results initialize an existing efficient method such as InfoMap for further quality refinement.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on public datasets at various scales reportedly show higher efficiency without significant quality degradation.
The authors report that online generalization and refinement improve inference efficiency by avoiding time-consuming model optimization.

narrative_sequence.summary: Community detection partitions graph nodes into densely connected groups.
Balancing community detection quality and efficiency remains difficult, particularly when the number of communities is unknown.
PRoCD reformulates K-agnostic community detection as binary node-pair classification within a pre-training and refinement paradigm.
The method is pre-trained on small synthetic graphs, transferred with frozen parameters to large real graphs, and used to initialize an efficient community detection method for refinement.
The authors report improved inference efficiency and no significant quality degradation on public datasets of various scales.

source_observation.claim: Offline pre-training on synthetic graphs is followed by frozen-parameter transfer and refinement on real graphs.

interpretation.claim: Separating expensive model optimization from online inference may support scalable transfer across graphs.

application.claim: For graph inference tasks with unknown structural parameters, consider synthetic pre-training plus initialization of an efficient existing solver.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy generalizes beyond the reported K-agnostic community detection setting or public datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training objectives, synthetic graph generation details, or hyperparameters.
The abstract does not report dataset names, quantitative efficiency measurements, quality metrics, baselines, or statistical comparisons.
The abstract does not describe failure cases, computational resource requirements, or sensitivity to graph topology.
